pr_body:
Block the cluster applier before disrupting the cluster so the victim
node doesn't try and rejoin too soon.

Closes #86974

review_comments: One question to understand this mock. Wouldn't this `addFailToSendNoConnectRule` prevent/drop reconnect attempts of the victim (to master)? How can the victim rejoin after this failure has been added to the transport service of master (and before it is cleared)?
No, this only prevents the master from sending/connecting to the victim, the connections in the opposite direction are unaffected.
... but also the victim was rejoining after this rule was cleared.

Hi @DaveCTurner , LGTM. I understand the issue that the victim might have sent the join request before making its network fail. However, I am still not sure why that was the reason that the second `barrier.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);` was the one timing out in the original issue's build scan ( https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/22kfr6xkperam/tests/:server:internalClusterTest/org.elasticsearch.discovery.DiscoveryDisruptionIT/testJoinWaitsForClusterApplier ) ? Even if the join request was sent earlier, shouldn't the barriers be passing either way? I would have expected a failure at `ensureStableCluster(2, masterName);` since the cluster would have 3 nodes instead of 2.

`ensureStableCluster(2, masterName)` waits for up to 30s for the cluster to have 2 nodes (by calling the cluster health API with a 30s timeout) and the barrier wait was timing out in this time. But then even if it didn't time out, `ensureStableCluster` throws an `AssertionError` eventually so we'd never get to the second `barrier.await` on the main test thread.

I think you should be able to reproduce this with the changes in [this comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/86974#issuecomment-1160314795).
